impact:
FINDING STRENGTHENED 2026-08-30 by running the actual matcher over the real corpus via the T-058 dashboard. The original diagnosis (the tool is rarely called) was correct but incomplete, and the fix direction it implied is wrong.

Measured over all 131 observations in ~/.zug/observations.jsonl:

  jaccard  shared  clusters  recurring(>=2)  promotable(>=3)  largest
   0.40      2       131          0                0            1     <- production today
   0.30      2       131          0                0            1
   0.25      2       130          1                0            2
   0.20      2       128          3                0            2
   0.15      2       127          4                0            2
   0.10      2       106         16                7            4

TWO RESULTS THAT CHANGE THE FIX:

1. At the production threshold, ALL 131 observations are mutually unique. So the gate is not merely under-called — even if zug_reinforce_observation fired on every single observation automatically, the matcher would still produce zero recurrences and zero lesson candidates. Adding a forcing function alone would change nothing. That was the originally proposed fix, and it would have shipped and appeared to work while producing exactly the same empty pipeline.

2. The sharedCount gate is dead code at every useful threshold. Sweeping sharedCount 1 vs 2 produces IDENTICAL numbers at every jaccard value tested — jaccard is always the binding constraint. The `sharedCount >= 2` half of the condition has never rejected anything the jaccard test did not already reject.

INTERPRETATION: lexical Jaccard is the wrong instrument for this corpus. These observations are long, richly-worded prose paragraphs; two statements of the same underlying pattern rarely share enough exact content words. Getting any promotable signal needs jaccard 0.10 — a 4x drop — at which point clustering is loose enough that it is grouping on incidental vocabulary, not meaning. There is no good operating point on this dial, which means the problem is not a mistuned threshold.

REVISED FIX DIRECTION (supersedes the original):
- Do NOT simply auto-call the existing matcher on a schedule. It would be a forcing function attached to an instrument that cannot detect the thing it is looking for.
- Compare something shorter and more canonical than the full paragraph — e.g. have zug_save_observation carry an explicit short pattern key, and match on that.
- Or replace lexical overlap with embedding similarity, where paraphrase actually scores as similar.
- Or have the agent name the pattern it thinks is recurring and match against named patterns rather than free text.
- Whatever is chosen, re-run the sweep against the real corpus before committing a threshold. The T-058 dashboard's Recurrence panel does this interactively.

ORIGINAL EVIDENCE (unchanged): reinforcements.jsonl holds 3 entries, all count 1, lastSeen 2026-06-25 / 2026-08-02 / 2026-08-30 — three calls in 192 sessions. getLessonCandidates(3) requires count >= 3, so the \"Lesson candidates\" block in the end_session response has never rendered and lessonCount is 0 across all 201 growth snapshots.
resolution:
FIXED in src/storage.ts and src/server.ts, following the REVISED direction — the one the T-058 dashboard forced. The original plan (auto-call the existing matcher) was implemented as its opposite, because the sweep proved it would have produced the same empty pipeline while appearing to work.

Two changes, because there were two defects — a broken instrument and a missing gate:

1. THE INSTRUMENT. Observation gains an optional `pattern` field: a short canonical name for the underlying trait ("verifies claims against primary sources"), supplied by the agent via a new optional parameter on zug_save_observation whose description specifies 3-8 words, present tense, no session specifics. Reinforcement now matches on THAT, never on the observation prose.

2. THE GATE. New autoReinforceSession(session_id) in storage.ts, called from runEndSession before the growth snapshot and the lesson-candidate check. Recurrence is computed from what was already recorded rather than depending on the agent remembering to call zug_reinforce_observation — which it did 3 times in 192 sessions.

Keys are deduped WITHIN a session, fuzzily, not just exactly: recurrence means across sessions, so one chatty session naming the same pattern three times must not promote it alone. Observations with no pattern key are SKIPPED, never matched on their prose.

VERIFICATION — end-to-end through the real runEndSession path, isolated temp data dir, no network. Three sessions each using a DIFFERENT phrasing of the key collapsed to one pattern at count 3 and surfaced the "Lesson candidates (reinforced 3+ times)" block, which has never rendered in 192 real sessions.

LIMITATION: the 131 existing observations carry no pattern key and cannot be backfilled without an LLM pass, so they stay skipped. The pipeline accumulates from the next session, not retroactively.

=== ADDENDUM: THRESHOLD ANALYSIS (see T-060) ===

This issue shipped the mechanism while leaving the inherited Jaccard 0.40 / sharedCount 2 gate in place. Asked what the threshold should actually be, it was measured against 18 labelled positive pairs and 200 negatives.

THE FIRST ANSWER WAS WRONG AND THE TEST SUITE CAUGHT IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH REMEMBERING. The initial labelled set contained only cross-group negatives — patterns semantically far apart. It reported 100% precision at every threshold and produced a confident recommendation of overlap 0.50 / sharedCount 2. Applying it broke an existing test: "First pattern reinforced more" and "Second pattern reinforced less" merged, sharing exactly 2 of a 4-word smaller set. The evaluation could not have found this, because the adversarial class was absent from it by construction. A clean 100% precision across every threshold should itself have been read as a warning that the negatives were too easy.

RE-MEASURED with adversarial negatives (same structure, discriminating word swapped). Precision collapses everywhere; no setting of either metric achieves both good recall and good precision. Like-for-like at equal 67% recall:

  jaccard 0.40 / 2 : precision 71%, 5 of 8 adversarial pairs wrongly merged
  overlap 0.50 / 3 : precision 86%, 2 of 8 adversarial pairs wrongly merged

Adopted overlap 0.50 / sharedCount 3. Two reasons: Jaccard's union denominator structurally caps unequal-length keys (a short key fully contained in a longer one cannot score high), and sharedCount — inert under Jaccard — is the half doing the work under overlap, lifting precision 70% -> 86%.

PRECISION IS 86%, NOT 100%. About one merge in seven is expected wrong, and the residual failures are semantic opposites no bag-of-words metric can separate. Acceptable only because getLessonCandidates surfaces candidates for review rather than creating lessons directly. All of this is provisional: it was derived from hand-authored phrasings because there are still zero real pattern keys in production.
title: Pattern reinforcement has no forcing function — 3 calls in 192 sessions, so the lesson pipeline is permanently empty
